result.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing Agentic Causal Discovery
result.summary: LLM agents can now run causal discovery algorithms on a dataset and report what comes out. Whether they do more than that, such as noticing where an algorithm went wrong and fixing it with further tests, is hard to tell from current benchmarks. Most of them give the variables meaningful names, and an LLM shown only the names of the Tübingen cause-effect pairs already gets 99% of the directions right. With the names removed, the data are usually clean enough that picking a better algorithm than PC closes most of the gap. We introduce Heuresis, a benchmark of anonymous simulated datasets whose mechanisms range from linear Gaussian to heavy-tailed. For each family of datasets it separates what a better existing algorithm can gain from what only a closer look at the data can gain, and it traces every edge an agent changes. Every family leaves a gap that none of the algorithms, the router and the two causal-discovery foundation models we ran can close, so a score above the best chosen algorithm has to come from using the data. We instantiate the benchmark with an agent harness and three LLMs, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and Qwen 3.8 Flash. GPT-6.1 Sol surpasses the best chosen algorithm on all six families, by 14% adjacency F1 on the most difficult one, and Claude Opus 5.5 does so by 7.4% there. A third of the true edges the two agents restore on the two hardest families appear in no algorithm's output. The code and data will be publicly released to facilitate future work.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Heuresis 基准：用去掉变量名的匿名模拟数据（机制从线性高斯到重尾）评测 LLM agent 能否不止于调用因果发现算法，而是察觉算法出错并用后续检验修正；并配 agent harness 与三个 LLM 给出结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其基准把「换更强的现有算法可得的收益」与「只能靠细看数据才能得的收益」显式分离，并逐条追踪 agent 改动的边，这一评测设计可能可供核查：用于区分 VLM/LVR 推理中源自语言或结构先验的旁路贡献与真正依赖视觉证据的贡献。
